summaries.export: Nothing in §14.1/§14.2/A5 exists as a feature. There is no ZIP or archive library in package.json (only sharp), no export, package or manifest tables, no output profiles, no publication intents, generations or acknowledgments, and no admin Publishing route under app/admin. The groundwork is the B05-m1 migration (20261113140000_media_b05m1_use_grants.sql). It adds a media_use_destinations registry (venue-scoped, internal or public audience, rows only via migration, none seeded), plus append-only media_use_grants and withdrawals. lib/server/media/use/grants.ts wraps these, but no UI calls it and it sits behind NABALENS_PUBLIC_USE_GRANTS, with the public derivative profiles (B05-m2) never built. The only downloads are the admin single-original route /api/media/[id]/download, which uses the uploader's original filename and records nothing, and evidence-document downloads. §14.3 is largely done as the internal reader API (app/api/knowledge/_reader, docs/knowledge/internal-reader-api.md). It returns structured answers with conditions, provenance, revision and freshness, and gives a typed unavailable reason for unknown or stale facts. Its audience is limited to internal. §17 notifications are missing entirely: no tables, preferences, quiet hours, digests, push or email. The closest things are in-app queues: staff Needs attention, the manager triage counts from manager_triage_summary, and the admin overview's setup flags. §18 is partial. venue_coverage_summary gives satisfied/applicable per venue, and OurMenuSection splits food and drinks with eligible/covered. A per-category split covering spaces and facilities, fact coverage, review delay, label correction rate by route, useful contributions, content use, reliability metrics and §18.3 product-analytics events are all missing (no PostHog or analytics code). The audit event tables (media_label_events, menu_item_photo_events, coverage_review_events, knowledge_events) could feed these metrics. The owner's decisions conflict mostly with wording. DESIGN.md §7 asks for "41 slots still empty", not "64% complete", and bans Published on staff screens. §9 bans toasts and leaderboards. All of these fit the spec if numerator/denominator and the Exported/Published states are kept to manager and admin screens, and in-app notifications are built as inbox or badge surfaces rather than toasts.
summaries.menus: The menu catalogue is solid. It has versioned drafts (menu_versions: draft, active, retired, discarded) and stable menu_items/menu_variants identities that are never shared between venues. Re-import matches only by source key, and a same-name match becomes an uncertain candidate that blocks activation until decided. Admin manual entry works (version-editor, menu-document-editor), and JSON/CSV import has row-numbered validation plus a preview diff of added, changed, removed, uncertain and unchanged items (/api/admin/menus/import-preview, MenuDiffView). Activating a version reconciles accepted item photos in the same transaction (reconcile_menu_item_photos). Price and meta changes leave photos alone; a name, section-kind or variant change sends a photo to needs_recheck. Spaces and facilities are covered by the amenity catalogue, venue_amenity_checks and knowledge_subjects places: answers are yes, no or not_applicable with a required reason, with a temporarily_unavailable qualifier, and capture-venue provenance is enforced by composite FKs. The biggest gaps are all things a manager cannot yet do or set: menu specials with dates, temporary sold-out, scheduled activation, future menus with photo preparation (an Upcoming slot), more than one menu per venue (one active version per venue and one entry per item per version, so AC22 fails), the group catalog and manager change-request queue (promote, merge, clarify, decline), cross-venue reuse proposals, a CSV template with the spec's columns (venue, menu name, stable ID, active dates), per-variant photo requirements, and a reason requirement when a manager archives an amenity check. There are two conflicts with owner decisions. Album sections are named Food, Drinks, Amenities, Areas, against the spec's Food, Drinks, Spaces, Facilities, Other. The Wi-Fi evidence rule 'both' needs a photo and a video, while the spec says a policy needs a photograph only when useful.
summaries.review: The manager workspace (/manager) has a working Overview, a Review list and Review-in-a-thumb (DESIGN.md §6.5), and per-dish detail with history. They run on security-definer RPCs: manager_menu_photo_overview/queue, review_menu_item_photo, assign_menu_item_photo, set_menu_item_primary_photo, withdraw_menu_item_photo and decide_area_photo. Several spec rules are already in place: revision-checked decisions (expectedRevision plus revision_conflict with fresh cards), fix-label-and-accept in one step (relink/assign through assign_menu_item_photo, which keeps corrects_item_id), atomic primary selection with an event history, a re-check when the dish name or section changes, and admin-only menu archiving. Overview shows the backlog with the oldest wait, items with no photo, items with a newer photo waiting, facts to confirm (Triage/To confirm) and the active menu. It keeps 'photos waiting' apart from 'items with no photo', but its coverage covers food and drinks menu sections only. It has no spaces/facilities coverage, no percentages, no publication issues and no reviewer assignment. Review keeps unlabelled photos under a separate 'Unlabelled photos' filter instead of the main queue. It has no task, age, media-type or duplicate filters, no batch decisions, no 'Keep as reference' state, no 'Mark duplicate' (media_assets has no content hash) and no capture date. Contributors are not notified when a reviewer fixes a label. Conflicts with spec: (a) manager self-review is blocked in the database (menu_item_photos_no_manager_self_review, decide_area_photo) and by DESIGN.md §6.5 'Nobody reviews their own photo', where the spec allows it at small venues; (b) the manager tabs are Overview/Review/Menu/Amenities, not Overview/Review/Album/Tasks/Venue; (c) Album's words ('41 slots still empty', not percentages; Accept/Ask again) and its reason chips differ from the spec's. M3 is the weakest section. Subject detail exists only for dishes and has no linked facts, tasks or destinations. Original download is admin-only (/api/media/[id]/download). Use-grant withdrawal (media_use_withdraw_asset) has no manager UI and is limited to listed granters. Nothing tracks 'external copy changed'.
summaries.admin: Admin today is five areas: Content (/admin library), Staff (/admin/staff), Menus (/admin/menus), Coverage (/admin/coverage group overview, per-venue tools, venue managers) and Albums (/admin/albums matrix), plus hidden routes for Search (/admin/search) and Knowledge (/admin/knowledge/*). There is no Venues, Publishing or Settings & activity area. A1 is partly there: getGroupOverview / coverage_group_overview give per-venue applicable/satisfied, needs-setup, to-review, overdue and menu-changed counts with a period (month) filter, and /admin/albums gives a Food/Drinks/Amenities/Areas matrix in name order with no ranking. Missing from A1: fact-coverage, unlabelled-backlog, oldest-review-age and publication-error columns, a blocked-first sort, venue/category/menu-version filters, and links from each number. A2 is missing: venues is a seed-only table (id, name, slug, active), with no create/edit UI, timezone, operating status, setup checklist, reviewer responsibility or archive. A4 is partial: the library filters by venue, contributor, media type, item/variant, category, content type, labelled state, text and upload date. /admin/search adds rights, destination and menu decision. Download and label correction work. There is no asset-detail page (provenance, renditions, approvals, usages), collections, controlled tags, duplicate comparison or archive/restore. Delete is an immediate tombstone with no reason or impact preview, which conflicts with §8 A4 and §16. Use-grant/withdraw server code exists (lib/server/media/use) but has no UI and sits behind NABALENS_PUBLIC_USE_GRANTS. A6 is partial: admin-only invite, deactivate (profile.active plus auth ban), reactivate, staff-to-manager conversion with reason and audit, and grant/revoke of venue managers. But the data model has a single profiles.venue_id and one open venue_manager_grant per person, so "manager at A, staff at B" (AC14) cannot be expressed. There is also no admin grant/revoke, no last-admin guard, no manager-initiated invite (AC40) and no bulk reassignment. A7 is mostly missing: limits are code constants (lib/config/media.ts) and there are no settings tables for reminders, retention, quiet hours or export formats. Audit rows exist (coverage_audit_events, menu_events, knowledge_events, media_label_events) but no activity screen reads them. Operational monitoring is limited to the R2 archive watchdog emails and the cleanup cron's stale-processing reaper; there is no admin view of stuck processing, failed exports/destinations or storage use. The owner's decisions on gallery-first, Match and staff tabs do not touch these admin sections. The no-leaderboard decision is consistent with the spec here: the existing staff-participation tallies are aggregate per venue and DESIGN.md §6.6 forbids ranking.
summaries.upload: The upload transport is solid and well tested. lib/upload (reserve, then TUS or signed PUT, then an idempotent finalise keyed by client_upload_key) has resumable TUS, per-file queue states with retry and cancel, a lost-response/409 path, an account-scoped IndexedDB capture journal, sign-out device cleanup and a log-out warning. Server finalise (lib/server/media/finalise.ts) checks bytes, signature, size and type, decodes once, writes WebP preview and thumb renditions with metadata stripped, and archives a verified original before the asset becomes ready. Labelling follows the owner's Album decisions rather than the spec's literal flows. From a slot, one gallery photo goes straight to that slot. From the Add photos tab, Match shows one photo at a time with up to 6 suggested empty slots, a search, Match later and Not for a slot. The older UploadDialog has one shared "What's in these photos?" field that applies to every file, with an Adjust option per file. The biggest gaps: (1) no explicit group labelling and no "same item / different items" question (§5.4, AC05), though Match's one-photo-at-a-time matching can be accepted as a reconciliation; (2) no "I'm not sure" state that sends a photo to a manager's Needs label queue, because Match later is private to the uploader (AC03); (3) no captured-date field, no duplicate check by content hash, and no blur, dark or resolution feedback; (4) launch limits differ from §12.1 (20 MiB photos, 200 MiB videos, no 60 s video limit, 10-file queue) and there is no video poster or preview; (5) processing runs inline in finalise, with no durable jobs and no rendition or processing-version records; (6) for staff, finalise and storage upload do not recheck that the uploader still belongs to the asset's venue, only that the account is active (AC12); (7) the server has no separate upload-batch or submission record; the state lives only in media_assets.upload_state. The spec's camera and record buttons, "Upload" wording and Home/Upload/Album/My uploads tabs conflict with D8/D9 and DESIGN.md §2 and §9. Keep the owner's decisions, which the spec allows since AC10 only needs the library route.
summaries.model: The schema already covers most of what §2, §10 and §11 ask for, but spread over several separate structures rather than one subject/requirement/usage model. Menu photos (menu_items, menu_entries, menu_versions, media_label_items, menu_item_photos with heads, events, a one-primary index and recheck on activation), facts (venue_amenity_checks, amenity_submissions and the knowledge_* layer with decisions, freshness and rechecks) and areas (knowledge_subjects, media_area_labels, area_photo_decisions) are solid. They keep append-only history, composite (id, venue_id) foreign keys, an immutable provenance snapshot and stale-write protection. Album (lib/album/model.ts) brings dishes, amenities and areas together in the app layer as slots with the states needed, sending, waiting, retake, accepted and not-here. The biggest gaps: no Reference approved vs Public approved split, so a single 'accepted' closes the requirement (invariant 4, AC16). There is no export/publication record or state machine; media_use_grants exists, but public grants are refused and destinations are inactive (AC31-33). There is no rendition table or derivative profiles, and no content hash or captured-time provenance on media_assets (AC20, AC21). There is no sold-out/availability state (AC26) and no presentation revision on offerings (AC19). There is no organisation table, venue timezone or group catalog, and no cross-venue reuse or provenance-correction path. Check due is not separate from Replacement needed for areas and amenities, and area photos have no review date at all (AC30). Fact freshness exists, but its policy table is seeded empty (OD-15), so Check due never fires. Two owner decisions conflict with the spec. Goals-not-tasks removed per-person menu tasks with due dates, which the spec's Task/brief record expects. D9 Match on add / Match later keeps unmatched photos on the phone and says nobody labels after sending, which conflicts with the spec's Needs label submission and its manager relabel without re-upload (AC03, AC15). Recommended reconciliations keep both owner decisions.
summaries.staff: The staff experience covered by §6 S1-S5 is built to the adopted Album design (DESIGN.md §5a, §6), not to the spec's four-tab layout. The tab bar is Album, Add photos and Me (components/nabalens/app-shell.tsx: ALBUM, AlbumAddTrigger, ME). Album at /staff/tasks is Home: it shows the venue's album count, the retake row, place chips, up to six empty slot tiles with an "All N" link to /staff/album/[placeId], Match later, Other jobs, Start here and one gallery-first main button. Add photos runs gallery, then Match (D9), with a per-file queue, resume and leave guard. Me (/staff, app/staff/staff-portfolio.tsx) holds the profile, Your month, Needs attention (label drafts), Needs labels, Accepted for menu use, retake notes (RetakeNotes, my_retake_notes), My contributions (per-item upload, label and review lines), the portfolio gallery with delete and label edit, and links to work details, the guide, Our menu, Photos and People. Log out is there too. Partial areas: Album only filters by place. There is no Needed / Awaiting review / Approved / Needs updating / All state filter, and needs_recheck dishes fold into Needed. Filled dish and area slots open nothing, so there is no staff subject page with approved material. A slot with someone else's pending photo reads Waiting and cannot take another contribution. There is no pending count on cards. Work-area preference exists (staff_work_profiles) but only orders the label picker, not Album or jobs. Me is not divided into the spec's Needs attention / Uploading / Awaiting review / Reviewed sections. Review outcome words cover Accepted, Waiting and Needs another photo, but not Kept as reference, Label corrected or Not used. Menu-photo retakes do not link to the earlier attempt; coverage retakes do (coverage_submission_items.replaces_item_id). The biggest gaps: no notification preferences or notifications of any kind, no photo-subject "Report a change" with the spec's five choices (it exists only for venue-question answers), no request-correction path for reviewed photos, no contact-manager route, and a single venue per staff profile (profiles.venue_id), so there are no assigned-venues lists or venue switching in Add. Conflicts with owner decisions: the tab set, gallery-first versus Take photo/Record video, Match-on-add versus post-send labelling and the spec's "change an unreviewed label", Album words versus spec outcome words ("Approved"), and the colleague Photos feed versus the spec's "private unreviewed media".
summaries.tasks: The task and venue-management pieces are spread across older layers, and nothing gives a manager one model or one screen for them. A media "task" today is just a coverage requirement: the `coverage_requirements` row is both the requirement and the task, with assignees in `coverage_requirement_assignees`. Facilities have per-venue amenity checks (`venue_amenity_checks`). Dishes carry a "needed by" date (`menu_item_needed_by`) and the album has one-line briefs (`album_briefs`). Retakes, approval-only completion and the rule that staff evidence never completes a fact are built and tested. Fact confirmation works through the knowledge layer: `knowledge_submit` / `knowledge_decide`, To confirm, freshness and rechecks. Two problems run through the rest. First, `/manager` is the canonical workspace (D3), yet `deny_manager_coverage_writes` blocks manager accounts from creating, assigning, cancelling or reviewing coverage requirements. So /manager has no way to create a task or brief, and non-menu task sends cannot be reviewed there. Second, the owner's 'Goals, not tasks' decisions (no owner, due date or overdue for menu work) and Album DESIGN.md §9 (no due or overdue states for slots) conflict with the spec's per-person, due-dated M4 tasks. Missing entirely: task types, priority, intended use, reference image, orientation, video, capture window, Blocked state, shot lists, optional versus required requests, local specials, menu sold-out or temporary availability, display-name overrides, manager invite and deactivate, main and backup reviewer assignments, a venue History screen and a single Venue hub. Membership is still one venue per profile, so 'manages A, staff at B' (AC14) cannot be modelled.
summaries.ux: The Album app (Next.js 16, Supabase RLS/RPCs, TUS uploads) already covers a lot of §15/§22. Accessibility checks exist: axe with wcag22aa tags in tests/e2e/responsive.spec.ts and menus-responsive.spec.ts, reflow at 320px and 200% plus forced colours in reflow.spec.ts, dark contrast, focus-obscured, 48px targets in DESIGN.md §3.4 and §8, and live regions on Match and the upload dialog. Upload reliability is strong: idempotency keys in lib/server/media/reserve.ts and finalise.ts, retry/lost-response/oversize tests in tests/integration/upload-recovery.test.ts, honest offline capability probing in lib/upload/capabilities.ts, and device clean-up on sign-out in lib/upload/device-cleanup.ts. Review concurrency (p_expected_revision), menu-revision rechecks, a single primary photo per dish, draft/active menus, CSV import and venue-scoped composite FKs cover several of AC13-AC28. There is no PWA at all: no app/manifest, no service worker, no install prompt. There are no manual exports, so AC31 and AC32 are missing from Release 1 scope. Managers cannot invite users (inviteStaff calls requireAdminCaller). The account model is one profiles.venue_id per person with one open venue_manager_grant, so AC14 (manager at A, staff at B) can't be expressed. Exact-file duplicates are not detected (no content hash on media_assets). Media editing/versioning and integrated withdrawal belong to Release 2. Performance targets from §15.2 have no measurements: Home 2.5 s, 30 s submission, label search p95. docs/perf covers only DB/library functions. Browser checks use Playwright webkit-phone emulation, and docs/qa/menus-qa-report.md admits there was no physical-device proof. There is no legacy media import for §20. Owner decisions conflict with the spec in four places: gallery-first vs camera/Retake wording, Album words vs 'Upload/Change label/Submit', Match one-at-a-time vs explicit batch groups (AC05), and Match later/Unlabelled photos vs a 'Needs label' item in the main queue (AC03). Each conflict below recommends keeping the owner's decision.
summaries.facts: The fact side of §9 is mostly built through B03 venue knowledge. There are append-only contributions, decisions and events, with one resolver (private.knowledge_slot_state_b03) that keeps answer values (yes/no/not_applicable) separate from verification status (available, not_confirmed, stale, disputed, withdrawn, unknown). Versioned value schemas exist for policy, accessibility, facility, service, schedule and Wi-Fi, along with change reports, corrections, withdrawals and import reconciliation. An internal reader at /api/knowledge/v1 never returns a value for an unconfirmed or stale answer. The freshness system is also built: knowledge_freshness_policies, read-time expiry or basis_missing, and recheck tasks. None of it is switched on yet. The policy table is seeded empty (OD-15), every key is still on registry version 1 (presence or connectivity.wifi), so the structured conditions and areas are not in use, and knowledge_run_rechecks has no cron or internal route.
